## A

### [abandon](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/abandon_1) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈbændən/` · **US:** `/əˈbændən/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/aba/aband/abandon__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/aba/aband/abandon__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - abandon somebody The baby had been abandoned by its mother.
  - People often simply abandon their pets when they go abroad.
  - abandon somebody to something ‘We have been abandoned to our fate,’ said one resident.
  - The study showed a deep fear among the elderly of being abandoned to the care of strangers.

### [absolute](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/absolute_1) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/ˈæbsəluːt/` · **US:** `/ˈæbsəluːt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/abs/absol/absolute__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/abs/absol/absolute__us_1_rr.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - I've joined a class for absolute beginners.
  - absolute confidence/trust/silence/truth
  - ‘You're wrong,’ she said with absolute certainty.
  - Clean water is an absolute necessity.
  - Around them the darkness was absolute, the silence oppressive.

### [absorb](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/absorb) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əbˈzɔːb/` · **US:** `/əbˈzɔːrb/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/abs/absor/absorb__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/abs/absor/absorb__us_2_rr.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - absorb something Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the air.
  - Let the rice cook until it has absorbed all the water.
  - absorb something into something The cream is easily absorbed into the skin.

### [abstract](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/abstract_1) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/ˈæbstrækt/` · **US:** `/ˈæbstrækt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/abs/abstr/abstract__gb_5.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/abs/abstr/abstract__us_2_rr.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - abstract knowledge/principles
  - The research shows that pre-school children are capable of thinking in abstract terms.

### [academic](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/academic_2) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˌækəˈdemɪk/` · **US:** `/ˌækəˈdemɪk/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/aca/acade/academic__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/aca/acade/academic__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - a leading/distinguished/prominent academic
  - There is much debate among academics about this issue.

### [accent](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/accent_1) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈæksənt/` · **US:** `/ˈæksənt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/acc/accen/accent__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/acc/accen/accent__us_1_rr.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - a northern/Dublin/Scottish accent
  - a strong/broad accent (= one that is easy to notice)
  - with an accent She spoke English with an accent.
  - The Americans had learned Korean and spoke with a good accent.

### [acceptable](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/acceptable) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/əkˈseptəbl/` · **US:** `/əkˈseptəbl/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/acc/accep/acceptable__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/acc/accep/acceptable__us_3.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Children must learn socially acceptable behaviour.
  - It is perfectly acceptable for you as an employee to say no.

### [accidentally](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/accidentally) *(adverb)*
- **UK:** `/ˌæksɪˈdentəli/` · **US:** `/ˌæksɪˈdentəli/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/acc/accid/accidentally__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/acc/accid/accidentally__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - As I turned around, I accidentally hit him in the face.
  - The damage couldn't have been caused accidentally.

### [accommodate](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/accommodate) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈkɒmədeɪt/` · **US:** `/əˈkɑːmədeɪt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/acc/accom/accommodate__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/acc/accom/accommodate__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The hotel can accommodate up to 500 guests.
  - The aircraft is capable of accommodating 28 passengers.

### [accompany](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/accompany) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈkʌmpəni/` · **US:** `/əˈkʌmpəni/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/acc/accom/accompany__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/acc/accom/accompany__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - accompany somebody/something + adv./prep. His wife accompanied him on the trip.
  - He was accompanied on the visit by his wife.
  - I must ask you to accompany me to the police station.
  - accompany somebody/something Warships will accompany the convoy.
  - The groups are always accompanied by an experienced mountain guide.
  - Each young person must be accompanied by an adult.

### [accomplish](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/accomplish) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈkʌmplɪʃ/` · **US:** `/əˈkɑːmplɪʃ/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/acc/accom/accomplish__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/acc/accom/accomplish__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The first part of the plan has been safely accomplished.
  - I don't feel I've accomplished very much today.
  - That's it. Mission accomplished (= we have done what we aimed to do).

### [account](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/account_2) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈkaʊnt/` · **US:** `/əˈkaʊnt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/acc/accou/account__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/acc/accou/account__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - be accounted + adj. In English law a person is accounted innocent until they are proved guilty.
  - be accounted + noun The event was accounted a success.

### [accountant](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/accountant) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/əˈkaʊntənt/` · **US:** `/əˈkaʊntənt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/acc/accou/accountant__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/acc/accou/accountant__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - We talked to the company’s chief accountant.
  - the investigating accountant’s report

### [accuracy](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/accuracy) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈækjərəsi/` · **US:** `/ˈækjərəsi/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/acc/accur/accuracy__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/acc/accur/accuracy__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - They questioned the accuracy of the information in the file.
  - Candidates are judged on technical accuracy as well as artistic expression.
  - She hits the ball with great accuracy.

### [accurate](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/accurate) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/ˈækjərət/` · **US:** `/ˈækjərət/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/acc/accur/accurate__gb_3.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/acc/accur/accurate__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - an accurate description/picture of something
  - Accurate measurements are essential.
  - I'm not convinced the reports are accurate.
  - The film is not historically accurate.
  - an accurate prediction/estimate/assessment
  - an accurate representation/portrayal
  - scientifically accurate information/data
  - reasonably/entirely/fairly accurate
  - The cost is an accurate reflection of the quality of our products.

### [accurately](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/accurately) *(adverb)*
- **UK:** `/ˈækjərətli/` · **US:** `/ˈækjərətli/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/acc/accur/accurately__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/acc/accur/accurately__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The article accurately reflects public opinion.
  - The report accurately reflects the current state of the industry.

### [accuse](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/accuse) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈkjuːz/` · **US:** `/əˈkjuːz/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/acc/accus/accuse__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/acc/accus/accuse__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - accuse somebody of something to accuse somebody of murder/a crime
  - accuse somebody of doing something She accused him of lying.
  - be accused of something The government was accused of incompetence.
  - to be falsely/wrongly/unjustly accused of something
  - (formal) They stand accused of crimes against humanity.

### [acid](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/acid_1) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈæsɪd/` · **US:** `/ˈæsɪd/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/aci/acid_/acid__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/aci/acid_/acid__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The acid burned a hole in her coat.
  - Stomach acids can break down the poison.
  - You will need a special chemical to neutralize the acid.

### [acknowledge](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/acknowledge) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əkˈnɒlɪdʒ/` · **US:** `/əkˈnɑːlɪdʒ/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/ack/ackno/acknowledge__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/ack/ackno/acknowledge__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - acknowledge something She refuses to acknowledge the need for reform.
  - I have to acknowledge the fact that I am partly responsible.
  - It's a generally acknowledged fact.
  - Most people acknowledge the existence of evil.
  - to openly/publicly/readily acknowledge something
  - acknowledge that… He does not acknowledge that he has done anything wrong.
  - acknowledge something to be, have, etc. something It is generally acknowledged to be true.

### [acquire](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/acquire) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈkwaɪə(r)/` · **US:** `/əˈkwaɪər/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/acq/acqui/acquire__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/acq/acqui/acquire__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - She has acquired a good knowledge of English.
  - How long will it take to acquire the necessary skills?
  - I would love to apply the newly acquired skills to a job that I enjoy.
  - He has acquired a reputation for dishonesty.
  - I have recently acquired a taste for olives.

### [activate](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/activate) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/ˈæktɪveɪt/` · **US:** `/ˈæktɪveɪt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/act/activ/activate__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/act/activ/activate__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The burglar alarm is activated by movement.
  - The gene is activated by a specific protein.

### [actual](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/actual) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/ˈæktʃuəl/` · **US:** `/ˈæktʃuəl/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/act/actua/actual__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/act/actua/actual__us_1_rr.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - James looks younger than his wife but in actual fact (= really) he is five years older.
  - The actual cost was higher than we expected.
  - The actual number of unemployed is more than 15 million.
  - What were his actual words?
  - A variety of factors could cause our actual results to differ from the expected results.
  - The story of the film is based on actual events and people.

### [adapt](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/adapt) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈdæpt/` · **US:** `/əˈdæpt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/ada/adapt/adapt__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/ada/adapt/adapt__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - It's amazing how soon you adapt.
  - The organisms were forced to adapt in order to survive.
  - adapt to something Some animals have a remarkable ability to adapt to changing environments.
  - A large organization can be slow to adapt to change
  - The company was able to adapt to the conditions and enhance its position.
  - We have had to adapt quickly to the new system.
  - adapt yourself to something It took him a while to adapt himself to his new surroundings.

### [addiction](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/addiction) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/əˈdɪkʃn/` · **US:** `/əˈdɪkʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/add/addic/addiction__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/add/addic/addiction__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - cocaine addiction
  - addiction to something He is now fighting his addiction to alcohol.
  - an addiction to TV game shows/social media/gambling

### [additional](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/additional) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/əˈdɪʃənl/` · **US:** `/əˈdɪʃənl/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/add/addit/additional__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/add/addit/additional__us_3.mp3)
- **Examples:**

- **UK:** `/ˈænjuəli/` · **US:** `/ˈænjuəli/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/ann/annua/annually__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/ann/annua/annually__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The exhibition is held annually.

### [anticipate](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/anticipate) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/ænˈtɪsɪpeɪt/` · **US:** `/ænˈtɪsɪpeɪt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/ant/antic/anticipate__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/ant/antic/anticipate__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - anticipate something We don't anticipate any major problems.
  - Our anticipated arrival time is 8.30.
  - The eagerly anticipated movie will be released next month.
  - anticipate doing something They anticipate moving to bigger premises by the end of the year.
  - anticipate something doing something I don't anticipate it being a problem.
  - anticipate that… We anticipate that sales will rise next year.
  - it is anticipated that… It is anticipated that inflation will stabilize at 3 per cent.

### [anxiety](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/anxiety) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/æŋˈzaɪəti/` · **US:** `/æŋˈzaɪəti/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/anx/anxie/anxiety__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/anx/anxie/anxiety__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - acute/intense/deep anxiety
  - Some hospital patients experience high levels of anxiety.
  - Waiting for exam results is a time of great anxiety.

### [anxious](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/anxious) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/ˈæŋkʃəs/` · **US:** `/ˈæŋkʃəs/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/anx/anxio/anxious__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/anx/anxio/anxious__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The bus was late and Sue began to get anxious.
  - anxious about something I felt very anxious and depressed about the future.
  - He seemed anxious about the meeting.
  - anxious for somebody Parents are naturally anxious for their children.

### [apology](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/apology) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/əˈpɒlədʒi/` · **US:** `/əˈpɑːlədʒi/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/apo/apolo/apology__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/apo/apolo/apology__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - to offer/make/demand/accept an apology
  - You owe him an apology for what you said.
  - We should like to offer our apologies for the delay to your flight today.
  - We received a letter of apology.

### [apparent](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/apparent) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/əˈpærənt/` · **US:** `/əˈpærənt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/app/appar/apparent__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/app/appar/apparent__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Their devotion was apparent.
  - Then, for no apparent reason, the train suddenly stopped.
  - apparent from something that… It was apparent from her face that she was really upset.
  - apparent to somebody that… It soon became apparent to everyone that he couldn't sing.
  - apparent that… It's readily apparent that she has a gift for this kind of writing.
  - apparent from something No damage was apparent from a brain scan.
  - apparent to somebody The consequences of our actions are not immediately apparent to us.

### [apparently](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/apparently) *(adverb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈpærəntli/` · **US:** `/əˈpærəntli/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/app/appar/apparently__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/app/appar/apparently__us_3.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Apparently they are getting divorced soon.
  - I thought she had retired, but apparently she hasn't.
  - He paused, apparently lost in thought.
  - The government was apparently unaware of the magnitude of the crisis.
  - The security forces were apparently taken by surprise.

### [appeal](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/appeal_1) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/əˈpiːl/` · **US:** `/əˈpiːl/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/app/appea/appeal__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/app/appea/appeal__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - appeal for something to launch a TV appeal for donations to the charity
  - appeal to somebody He made an emotional appeal to voters.
  - appeal to somebody for something Police are making a fresh appeal to the public for any information that may help them.
  - appeal to somebody to do something The police made an appeal to the public to remain calm.
  - There was a look of silent appeal on his face.

### [appeal](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/appeal_2) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈpiːl/` · **US:** `/əˈpiːl/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/app/appea/appeal__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/app/appea/appeal__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - I am appealing (= asking for money) on behalf of the famine victims.
  - appeal for something Community leaders appealed for calm (= urged people to remain calm).
  - appeal to somebody Appeal directly to the public, answer their questions.
  - appeal to somebody for something The government appealed to the British people for help.
  - appeal for somebody to do something Police have appealed for witnesses to come forward.
  - appeal to somebody to do something Organizers appealed to the crowd not to panic.

### [applicant](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/applicant) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈæplɪkənt/` · **US:** `/ˈæplɪkənt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/app/appli/applicant__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/app/appli/applicant__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - There were over 500 applicants for the job.
  - Successful applicants will receive notification within the week.

### [approach](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/approach_1) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/əˈprəʊtʃ/` · **US:** `/əˈprəʊtʃ/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/app/appro/approach__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/app/appro/approach__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - She took the wrong approach in her dealings with them.
  - It was time to take a different approach.
  - an alternative/innovative approach
  - a traditional/similar approach
  - The approach they were using no longer seemed to work.
  - approach to something We need to adopt a new approach to the problem.
  - The therapy takes a holistic approach to health and well-being.
  - approach for something a variety of approaches for the treatment of depression
  - approach for doing something Will this be a successful approach for providing high-tech offices?

### [approach](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/approach_2) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈprəʊtʃ/` · **US:** `/əˈprəʊtʃ/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/app/appro/approach__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/app/appro/approach__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - We could hear the train approaching.
  - Winter is approaching.
  - The deadline was fast approaching.
  - The rapidly approaching storm could be seen on the horizon.
  - approach somebody/something She's approaching the end of her first year in the job.
  - I was approached by a woman who asked for the time.
  - The house is approached via a long driveway.
  - approach (somebody/something) from… The men approached the creature cautiously from behind.

### [appropriate](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/appropriate_1) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/əˈprəʊpriət/` · **US:** `/əˈprəʊpriət/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/app/appro/appropriate__gb_4.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/app/appro/appropriate__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - an appropriate response/measure/method
  - Now that the problem has been identified, appropriate action can be taken.
  - Is now an appropriate time to make a speech?
  - Please debit my Mastercard/Visa/American Express card (delete as appropriate) (= cross out the options that do not apply).
  - This may be an appropriate treatment for many patients.
  - Skills can be enhanced by the appropriate use of technology in certain circumstances.
  - He said she had responded to the situation in an entirely appropriate way.
  - to deem/consider/think something appropriate
  - appropriate for something Jeans are not appropriate for a formal party.
  - appropriate to something The book was written in a style appropriate to the age of the children.
  - All personnel were trained at levels appropriate to the needs of each job.

### [appropriately](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/appropriately) *(adverb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈprəʊpriətli/` · **US:** `/əˈprəʊpriətli/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/app/appro/appropriately__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/app/appro/appropriately__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The government has been accused of not responding appropriately to the needs of the homeless.
  - The chain of volcanoes is known, appropriately enough, as the ‘Ring of Fire’.

### [approval](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/approval) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/əˈpruːvl/` · **US:** `/əˈpruːvl/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/app/appro/approval__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/app/appro/approval__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - She desperately wanted to win her father's approval.
  - Do the plans meet with your approval?
  - in approval Several people nodded in approval.
  - The president's approval ratings were slipping.

### [approve](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/approve) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈpruːv/` · **US:** `/əˈpruːv/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/app/appro/approve__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/app/appro/approve__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - I told my mother I wanted to leave school but she didn't approve.
  - approve of somebody/something Do you approve of my idea?
  - She didn't quite approve of the way he was running things.
  - approve of somebody doing something She doesn't approve of me leaving school this year.
  - (formal) approve of somebody’s doing something She doesn't approve of my leaving school this year.

### [arise](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/arise) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈraɪz/` · **US:** `/əˈraɪz/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/ari/arise/arise__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/ari/arise/arise__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - An opportunity arose to work in the United States.
  - Questions naturally arose as to who was responsible.
  - A serious problem can arise if the heart stops pumping effectively.
  - Children should be disciplined when the need arises (= when it is necessary).
  - This issue arose as an unintended consequence of the Act.
  - A new crisis has arisen.
  - We keep them informed of any changes as they arise.
  - A storm arose during the night.

### [armed](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/armed) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/ɑːmd/` · **US:** `/ɑːrmd/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/arm/armed/armed__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/arm/armed/armed__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - an armed robbery
  - an international armed conflict (= a war)
  - Guerrillas have pledged to intensify the armed struggle against the new government.

### [arms](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/arms) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ɑːmz/` · **US:** `/ɑːrmz/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/arm/arms_/arms__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/arm/arms_/arms__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - arms and ammunition
  - The UN imposed an arms embargo on the country.
  - He's the world's most notorious arms dealer.
  - Police officers in the UK do not usually carry arms.
  - They banned arms sales to countries with poor human rights records.
  - He was trying to rebuild the country's nuclear arms programme.

### [arrow](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/arrow) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈærəʊ/` · **US:** `/ˈærəʊ/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/arr/arrow/arrow__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/arr/arrow/arrow__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - a bow and arrow
  - to fire/shoot an arrow
  - The road continues as straight as an arrow.

### [artificial](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/artificial) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/ˌɑːtɪˈfɪʃl/` · **US:** `/ˌɑːrtɪˈfɪʃl/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/art/artif/artificial__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/art/artif/artificial__us_3.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - an artificial limb/flower/sweetener/fertilizer
  - artificial lighting/light

### [artistic](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/artistic) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/ɑːˈtɪstɪk/` · **US:** `/ɑːrˈtɪstɪk/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/art/artis/artistic__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/art/artis/artistic__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - the artistic works of the period
  - a work of great artistic merit
  - an artistic temperament (= behaviour thought to be typical of artists, musicians, etc.)
  - Love is a time-honoured subject of literary and artistic expression.

### [artwork](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/artwork) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈɑːtwɜːk/` · **US:** `/ˈɑːrtwɜːrk/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/art/artwo/artwork__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/art/artwo/artwork__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Can you let me have the finished artwork for the poster by Friday?

### [ashamed](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/ashamed) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/əˈʃeɪmd/` · **US:** `/əˈʃeɪmd/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/ash/asham/ashamed__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/ash/asham/ashamed__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - ashamed of something She was deeply ashamed of her behaviour at the party.
  - Feeling depressed is nothing to be ashamed of.
  - We must stop being afraid or ashamed of what we are.
  - ashamed of somebody His daughter looked such a mess that he was ashamed of her.
  - ashamed of yourself You should be ashamed of yourself for telling such lies.
  - You ought to be thoroughly ashamed of yourselves.
  - ashamed that… I feel almost ashamed that I've been so lucky.
  - ashamed to be something The football riots made me ashamed to be English.

### [aside](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/aside_1) *(adverb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈsaɪd/` · **US:** `/əˈsaɪd/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/asi/aside/aside__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/asi/aside/aside__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - She pulled the curtain aside.
  - Stand aside and let these people pass.
  - He took me aside (= away from a group of people) to give me some advice.
  - (figurative) Leaving aside (= not considering at this stage) the cost of the scheme, let us examine its benefits.
  - All our protests were brushed aside (= ignored).

### [aspect](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/aspect) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈæspekt/` · **US:** `/ˈæspekt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/asp/aspec/aspect__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/asp/aspec/aspect__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - aspect of something The book aims to cover all aspects of city life.
  - The exhibition will focus on various aspects of life and culture in the Middle East.
  - the most important aspect of the debate
  - She felt she had looked at the problem from every aspect.
  - This was one aspect of her character he hadn't seen before.
  - We have worked very hard on certain aspects of our game.
  - The consultancy gives advice to manufacturers on the health and safety aspects of their products.

### [assess](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/assess) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈses/` · **US:** `/əˈses/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/ass/asses/assess__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/ass/asses/assess__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - assess somebody/something Accurately assessing environmental impacts is very complex.
  - to assess a patient’s needs
  - It's difficult to assess the effects of these changes.
  - Interviews allow you to assess the suitability of candidates.
  - She engaged a safety consultant to assess the risks.
  - Quality of life was assessed using a questionnaire.
  - assess somebody/something as something The young men were assessed as either safe or unsafe drivers.
  - I'd assess your chances as low.
  - assess whether, how, etc… The committee assesses whether a building is worth preserving.
  - We are trying to assess how well the system works.

### [assessment](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/assessment) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/əˈsesmənt/` · **US:** `/əˈsesmənt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/ass/asses/assessment__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/ass/asses/assessment__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - a detailed assessment of the risks involved
  - An adequate environmental impact assessment was not carried out on the bypass project.
  - We conducted the initial assessments defining the scope of work.
  - The city hired them to do a structural assessment of the damage.
  - his assessment of the situation

### [asset](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/asset) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈæset/` · **US:** `/ˈæset/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/ass/asset/asset__gb_3.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/ass/asset/asset__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - In his job, patience is an invaluable asset.
  - Being able to speak a foreign language is a major asset.
  - I’m not sure if his forcefulness is an asset or a liability.
  - asset to somebody/something She'll be an asset to the team.

### [assign](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/assign) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈsaɪn/` · **US:** `/əˈsaɪn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/ass/assig/assign__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/ass/assig/assign__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - assign something (to somebody) The teacher assigned a different task to each of the children.
  - The two large classrooms have been assigned to us.
  - assign somebody something We have been assigned the two large classrooms.
  - The teacher assigned each of the children a different task.

### [assistance](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/assistance) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/əˈsɪstəns/` · **US:** `/əˈsɪstəns/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/ass/assis/assistance__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/ass/assis/assistance__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - technical/economic/military assistance
  - financial assistance for people on low incomes
  - Can I be of any assistance?
  - Despite his cries, no one came to his assistance.
  - The other passengers went to her assistance.
  - with the assistance of somebody/something He can only walk with the assistance of crutches.
  - assistance with something She offered me practical assistance with my research.
  - assistance in doing something/to do something The company provides advice and assistance in finding work.

### [associate](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/associate_1) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈsəʊʃieɪt/` · **US:** `/əˈsəʊʃieɪt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/ass/assoc/associate__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/ass/assoc/associate__us_2_rr.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - associate somebody/something with somebody/something I always associate the smell of baking with my childhood.
  - He is closely associated in the public mind with horror movies.
  - Most people immediately associate addictions with drugs, alcohol and cigarettes.
  - associate somebody/something You wouldn’t normally associate these two writers—their styles are completely different.

### [associated](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/associated) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/əˈsəʊʃieɪtɪd/` · **US:** `/əˈsəʊʃieɪtɪd/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/ass/assoc/associated__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/ass/assoc/associated__us_4.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - associated with doing something the risks associated with taking drugs
  - associated with something Exposure to the sun is strongly associated with an increase in the incidence of skin cancer.
  - The conference will address the broad issues associated with E-commerce.
  - The following factors were significantly associated with chronic fatigue.
  - Lack of confidence is not something normally associated with a high-flying sales executive.

### [assume](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/assume) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈsjuːm/` · **US:** `/əˈsuːm/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/ass/assum/assume__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/ass/assum/assume__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - assume (that)… It is reasonable to assume (that) the economy will continue to improve.
  - It's probably safe to assume (that) we'll be hearing more about this story.
  - Let us assume for a moment that the plan succeeds.
  - She would, he assumed, be home at the usual time.
  - it is assumed (that)… It is generally assumed that stress is caused by too much work.
  - assume something Don't always assume the worst (= that something bad has happened).
  - In this example we have assumed a unit price of $10.
  - assume somebody/something to be/have something I had assumed him to be a Belgian.

### [assumption](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/assumption) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/əˈsʌmpʃn/` · **US:** `/əˈsʌmpʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/ass/assum/assumption__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/ass/assum/assumption__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - an underlying/implicit assumption
  - We need to challenge some of the basic assumptions of Western philosophy.
  - We are working on the assumption that everyone invited will turn up.
  - It was impossible to make assumptions about people's reactions.
  - His actions were based on a false assumption.
  - She arrived at college with a whole set of assumptions inherited from her family.

### [assure](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/assure) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈʃɔː(r)/` · **US:** `/əˈʃʊr/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/a/ass/assur/assure__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/a/ass/assur/assure__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - assure somebody (that)… You think I did it deliberately, but I assure you (that) I did not.
  - Let me assure you that I will try to help you.
  - We were assured that everything possible was being done.
  - She's perfectly safe, I can assure you.
  - assure somebody (of something) We assured him of our support.
  - I won’t let you down, I can assure you of that.
  - assure somebody + speech ‘He'll come back,’ Susan assured her.

### [attempt](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/attempt_1) *(noun)*

  - attempt at something The couple made an unsuccessful attempt at a compromise.
  - attempt at doing something They were praised for making an attempt at solving the problem.

### [attempt](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/attempt_2) *(verb)*

### [bet](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/bet_1) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/bet/` · **US:** `/bet/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/b/bet/bet__/bet__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/b/bet/bet__/bet__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**

  - bet on/against something He likes betting on horses and watching table tennis.
  - bet something on something He bet $2 000 on the final score of the game.
  - bet something You shouldn't praise a gambler for betting his life savings if he wins.
  - bet somebody something (that) She bet me £20 (that) I wouldn't do it.
  - bet somebody (that) I bet her (that) the Democrats would not win.
  - bet something (that) He bet ten dollars (that) he could write a complete story in just six words.

### [chase](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/chase_1) *(verb)*

- **UK:** `/ˈsɜːkəmstæns/` · **US:** `/ˈsɜːrkəmstæns/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/c/cir/circu/circumstance__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/c/cir/circu/circumstance__us_3.mp3)
- **Examples:**

  - Britain is fortunately not facing the same set of circumstances.
  - The court will take into account all the circumstances of the case.
  - Police are investigating the circumstances of the death of a baby boy.

### [cite](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/cite) *(verb)*

- **Examples:**

  - There is no reason to doubt the information in the articles cited above.
  - He cited personal reasons for his decision to resign.

  - Their method is similar to those used by many studies cited in this report.
  - cite something as something He cited his heavy workload as the reason for his breakdown.

### [citizen](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/citizen) *(noun)*

### [comfort](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/comfort_1) *(noun)*

  - I didn't want to leave the comfort of my bed.

  - for comfort I dress for comfort rather than elegance.
  - These tennis shoes are designed for comfort and performance.
  - He's beginning to find a comfort level with his teammates now.

### [comfort](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/comfort_2) *(verb)*

  - The idea that he was not alone comforted him greatly.
  - I am comforted by the fact that Jamie died doing what he liked best.
  - comfort yourself with something She comforted herself with the thought that it would soon be spring.
  - be comforted to do something He was comforted to know that most people in the class knew even less than he.
  - it comforts somebody to do something It comforted her to feel his arms around her.

### [comic](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/comic_1) *(adjective)*

### [command](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/command_1) *(noun)*

- **Examples:**

### [command](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/command_2) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/kəˈmɑːnd/` · **US:** `/kəˈmænd/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/c/com/comma/command__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/c/com/comma/command__us_2.mp3)

  - command that… (formal) The commission intervened and commanded that work on the building cease.

### [commander](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/commander) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/kəˈmɑːndə(r)/` · **US:** `/kəˈmændər/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/c/com/comma/commander__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/c/com/comma/commander__us_1.mp3)

### [commission](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/commission_1) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/kəˈmɪʃn/` · **US:** `/kəˈmɪʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/c/com/commi/commission__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/c/com/commi/commission__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The commission is expected to report its findings next month.
  - (British English) The government has set up a commission of inquiry into the disturbances at the prison.
  - The election commission found that neither candidate received enough votes to avoid a run-off.
  - on a commission the British representative on the commission
  - before a commission The defendant will be brought to trial before a military commission.
  - commission on something She was also a member of the commission on religious education.
  - a commission on human rights
  - The government appointed an independent commission to investigate the causes of the disaster.

### [commission](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/commission_2) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/kəˈmɪʃn/` · **US:** `/kəˈmɪʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/c/com/commi/commission__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/c/com/commi/commission__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - commission somebody to do something She has been commissioned to write a new national anthem.
  - commission something to commission a study/report
  - a specially commissioned piece of music
  - Publishers have commissioned a French translation of the book.
  - The survey on consumer taste was commissioned by local stores.
  - commission something from somebody The king commissioned portraits from foreign artists.
  - commission something for something the first opera commissioned for television

### [commitment](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/commitment) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/kəˈmɪtmənt/` · **US:** `/kəˈmɪtmənt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/c/com/commi/commitment__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/c/com/commi/commitment__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - I'm not ready to make a long-term commitment.
  - They have failed to honour their commitments.
  - commitment to somebody/something The company has shown a commitment to diversity over the years.
  - He questioned the government's commitment to public services.
  - We're looking for a firm commitment from both sides.
  - commitment to do/doing something This project demonstrates our commitment to improving the quality of the city's green spaces.
  - They reaffirmed their commitment to work for peace.
  - commitments under something Australia is determined to meet its commitments under the agreement.

### [committee](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/committee) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/kəˈmɪti/` · **US:** `/kəˈmɪti/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/c/com/commi/committee__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/c/com/commi/committee__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - an executive/advisory/organizing committee
  - a parliamentary/congressional/Senate committee
  - The committee has/have decided to close the restaurant.
  - The committee unanimously approved the plan.
  - to appoint/establish/form a committee
  - to chair/head a committee
  - on a committee She's on the planning committee.
  - He has served on numerous committees.
  - I have been invited to sit on the committee.
  - before a committee He will be called to give evidence before the committee.
  - in committee The bill was still in committee (= being considered by a committee) in early December.
  - committee of somebody/something a committee of inquiry
  - a committee of MPs/experts
  - committee to do something A special committee to investigate the possible impeachment of the governor meets later today.
  - committee on something the US House of Representatives' committee on foreign affairs
  - a committee member/chairman
  - a committee meeting/report
  - the chairman/chair of a committee
  - a member/meeting of a committee

### [commonly](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/commonly) *(adverb)*
- **UK:** `/ˈkɒmənli/` · **US:** `/ˈkɑːmənli/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/c/com/commo/commonly__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/c/com/commo/commonly__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**

  - symptoms commonly associated with HIV
  - These fats are commonly found in processed foods.
  - one of the most commonly available substances on the planet

### [comparative](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/comparative_1) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/kəmˈpærətɪv/` · **US:** `/kəmˈpærətɪv/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/c/com/compa/comparative__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/c/com/compa/comparative__us_1.mp3)

### [completion](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/completion) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/kəmˈpliːʃn/` · **US:** `/kəmˈpliːʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/c/com/compl/completion__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/c/com/compl/completion__us_1.mp3)

### [complex](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/complex_2) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈkɒmpleks/` · **US:** `/ˈkɑːmpleks/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/c/com/compl/complex__gb_3.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/c/com/compl/complex__us_4.mp3)

### [complicated](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/complicated) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/ˈkɒmplɪkeɪtɪd/` · **US:** `/ˈkɑːmplɪkeɪtɪd/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/c/com/compl/complicated__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/c/com/compl/complicated__us_3.mp3)

### [component](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/component_1) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/kəmˈpəʊnənt/` · **US:** `/kəmˈpəʊnənt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/c/com/compo/component__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/c/com/compo/component__us_1.mp3)

  - the components of a machine
  - component for something Individual components for the car can be very expensive.

  - Component failure was the cause of the accident.

- **UK:** `/kəmˈpʌlsəri/` · **US:** `/kəmˈpʌlsəri/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/c/com/compu/compulsory__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/c/com/compu/compulsory__us_1.mp3)

- **UK:** `/ˌkɒnsnˈtreɪʃn/` · **US:** `/ˌkɑːnsnˈtreɪʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xconc/xconcentration__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xconc/xconcentration__us_1.mp3)

- **UK:** `/ˈkɒnsept/` · **US:** `/ˈkɑːnsept/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xconc/xconcept__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xconc/xconcept__us_1.mp3)

### [concern](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/concern_2) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈsɜːn/` · **US:** `/kənˈsɜːrn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xconc/xconcern__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xconc/xconcern__us_3.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - concern about something/somebody Villagers expressed concern about the level of traffic.
  - There is growing concern about violence in the media.
  - concern over something/somebody The report raises serious concerns over safety at the plant.
  - concern for something/somebody She hasn't been seen for four days and there is concern for her safety.
  - to raise/voice concerns

  - Don't hesitate to ask if you have any questions or concerns.
  - concern among somebody The school's recent examination results have sparked concern among parents.
  - concern that… There is widespread concern that new houses will be built on protected land.
  - security/safety concerns
  - He had to resign from his job because of health concerns.
  - The president's health was giving serious cause for concern.
  - The continuing drought is causing concern among farmers.
  - concern to somebody This is a matter of grave concern to our members.
  - with concern We view these developments with concern.
  - something is of concern The cost of the scheme is of major concern.

### [concern](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/concern_1) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈsɜːn/` · **US:** `/kənˈsɜːrn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xconc/xconcern__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xconc/xconcern__us_3.mp3)
- **Examples:**

  - To whom it may concern… (= used for example, at the beginning of a public notice or of a job reference about somebody’s character and ability)
  - Please pay attention because this information concerns all of you.
  - The letter is for both of us, but it mainly concerns you.

### [concerned](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/concerned) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈsɜːnd/` · **US:** `/kənˈsɜːrnd/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xconc/xconcerned__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xconc/xconcerned__us_3.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Concerned citizens can have a huge impact.
  - concerned parents/residents/parents/locals
  - concerned about something/somebody The president is deeply concerned about this issue.
  - We are extremely concerned about her.
  - concerned for something/somebody He didn't seem in the least concerned for her safety.
  - We were concerned for his welfare.
  - I told him but he didn't seem overly concerned (= he was not very concerned)
  - concerned (that)… She was concerned that she might miss the turning and get lost.
  - concerned over something Local residents are concerned over the impact of the project.
  - concerned at something I was rather concerned at the severity of the punishment.
  - concerned by something Her parents are growing increasingly concerned by her erratic behaviour.
  - a concerned look/glance

### [concrete](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/concrete_2) *(noun)*

### [conduct](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/conduct_1) *(verb)*

### [confess](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/confess) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈfes/` · **US:** `/kənˈfes/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xconf/xconfess__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xconf/xconfess__us_1.mp3)
