  - confess your crime, error, etc. We persuaded her to confess her crime.

### [confidence](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/confidence) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈkɒnfɪdəns/` · **US:** `/ˈkɑːnfɪdəns/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xconf/xconfidence__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xconf/xconfidence__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The president's actions hardly inspire confidence.
  - confidence in somebody/something The players all have confidence in their manager.
  - He believes his reforms will restore confidence in the financial markets.
  - The survey revealed a lack of confidence in the government.
  - She has the utmost confidence in her students' abilities.
  - Our aim is to increase public confidence in the democratic process.
  - The university is facing a crisis of confidence about its future role.
  - The new contracts have undermined the confidence of employees.

### [conflict](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/conflict_1) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈkɒnflɪkt/` · **US:** `/ˈkɑːnflɪkt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xconf/xconflict__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xconf/xconflict__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The violence was the result of political conflicts.
  - conflict between A and B (over something) a conflict between two cultures
  - His task will be to resolve potential conflicts between the British and Scottish governments.
  - conflict with somebody The prime minister wants to avoid conflict with the unions.
  - conflict over something The government has done nothing to resolve the conflict over nurses' pay.
  - in conflict with somebody (over something) She found herself in conflict with her parents over her future career.
  - John often comes into conflict with his boss.
  - conflict within something The terms of the will became a source of conflict within the family.
  - She has received training in conflict resolution.

### [conflict](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/conflict_2) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈflɪkt/` · **US:** `/kənˈflɪkt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xconf/xconflict__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xconf/xconflict__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Reports conflicted on how much of the aid was reaching the famine victims.
  - There are several major areas where their interests conflict.
  - conflict with something These results conflict with earlier findings.

### [confusing](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/confusing) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈfjuːzɪŋ/` · **US:** `/kənˈfjuːzɪŋ/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xconf/xconfusing__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xconf/xconfusing__us_3.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The instructions on the box are very confusing.
  - a confusing situation/experience
  - confusing messages/signals
  - a confusing array of options
  - This is where it all starts to get really confusing.
  - Beginners may find the terminology confusing.
  - confusing for somebody The new signs will be very confusing for tourists.
  - confusing to somebody All this information can be confusing to the user.
  - confusing to do The site is somewhat confusing to navigate.
  - it is confusing (for/to somebody) to do something It would be confusing to have two sets of regulations for a single country.

### [confusion](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/confusion) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈfjuːʒn/` · **US:** `/kənˈfjuːʒn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xconf/xconfusion__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xconf/xconfusion__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The announcement caused a lot of confusion.
  - confusion about/over something There is some confusion about what the correct procedure should be.
  - confusion as to something There was a confusion as to what to do next.

### [conscious](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/conscious) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/ˈkɒnʃəs/` · **US:** `/ˈkɑːnʃəs/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconscious__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconscious__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - conscious of something She's very conscious of the problems involved.
  - I am conscious of the fact that there's a limit to what we can achieve here.
  - conscious of doing something He became acutely conscious of having failed his parents.
  - conscious that… I was vaguely conscious that I was being watched.

### [consequently](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/consequently) *(adverb)*
- **UK:** `/ˈkɒnsɪkwəntli/` · **US:** `/ˈkɑːnsɪkwentli/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsequently__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsequently__us_1_rr.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - This poses a threat to agriculture and the food chain, and consequently to human health.
  - She failed her exams and was consequently unable to start her studies at college.

### [conservation](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/conservation) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˌkɒnsəˈveɪʃn/` · **US:** `/ˌkɑːnsərˈveɪʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconservation__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconservation__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - to be interested in wildlife conservation
  - Road development in the area has been limited by conservation programmes.

### [conservative](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/conservative_1) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈsɜːvətɪv/` · **US:** `/kənˈsɜːrvətɪv/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconservative__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconservative__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - the conservative views of his parents
  - music which is accessible to an audience with extremely conservative tastes
  - The southern state's inhabitants tend to be socially conservative.
  - Her style of dress was never conservative.
  - conservative in something They were deeply conservative in their outlook.

### [conservative](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/conservative_2) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈsɜːvətɪv/` · **US:** `/kənˈsɜːrvətɪv/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconservative__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconservative__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - social/religious conservatives
  - The former Texas Supreme Court Justice's moderate record has angered hard-line conservatives for years.

### [considerable](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/considerable) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈsɪdərəbl/` · **US:** `/kənˈsɪdərəbl/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsiderable__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsiderable__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The project wasted a considerable amount of time and money.
  - Damage to the building was considerable.
  - Considerable progress has been made in finding a cure for the disease.

### [considerably](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/considerably) *(adverb)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈsɪdərəbli/` · **US:** `/kənˈsɪdərəbli/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsiderably__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsiderably__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The need for sleep varies considerably from person to person.
  - Interest rates on bank loans have increased considerably in recent years.
  - Pollution levels have considerably reduced in this time.
  - Prices are considerably higher than they were a year ago.

### [consideration](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/consideration) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/kənˌsɪdəˈreɪʃn/` · **US:** `/kənˌsɪdəˈreɪʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsideration__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsideration__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - An employer is legally bound to give due consideration to the request.
  - Careful consideration should be given to issues of health and safety.
  - Her ideas are worthy of serious consideration.
  - to merit/deserve/warrant further consideration
  - After a few moments' consideration, he began to speak.
  - There needs to be a consideration of the legal issues involved.
  - under consideration The proposals are currently under consideration (= being discussed).
  - for (somebody's) consideration I enclose the report for your consideration.
  - for consideration by somebody The group have submitted two resolutions for consideration by shareholders.

### [consistent](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/consistent) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈsɪstənt/` · **US:** `/kənˈsɪstənt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsistent__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsistent__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - a consistent approach to the problem
  - a consistent pattern of behaviour
  - He has been Milan's most consistent player (= who plays well most often) this season.
  - consistent in something She's not very consistent in the way she treats her children.
  - consistent in doing something We must be consistent in applying the rules.

### [consistently](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/consistently) *(adverb)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈsɪstəntli/` · **US:** `/kənˈsɪstəntli/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsistently__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsistently__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Her work has been of a consistently high standard.

### [conspiracy](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/conspiracy) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈspɪrəsi/` · **US:** `/kənˈspɪrəsi/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconspiracy__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconspiracy__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - conspiracy (to do something) a conspiracy to overthrow the government
  - They were charged with conspiracy to murder.
  - conspiracy against somebody/something conspiracies against the president
  - a conspiracy of silence (= an agreement not to talk publicly about something that should be made public)

### [constant](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/constant_1) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/ˈkɒnstənt/` · **US:** `/ˈkɑːnstənt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconstant__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconstant__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - There were constant interruptions.
  - a constant stream of visitors all day
  - The ruined buildings serve as a constant reminder of the war.
  - The constant threat of violence from the other inmates was hard to deal with.
  - Doctors are under constant pressure to treat more and more patients.
  - Babies need constant attention.
  - This entrance is in constant use.

### [constantly](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/constantly) *(adverb)*
- **UK:** `/ˈkɒnstəntli/` · **US:** `/ˈkɑːnstəntli/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconstantly__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconstantly__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Fashion is constantly changing.
  - I am constantly reminded how fortunate I am.
  - We are constantly looking for ways to improve our products.
  - We are constantly on the lookout for new ideas.
  - Heat the sauce, stirring constantly.
  - You have to be constantly aware of your surroundings when walking home late at night.

### [construct](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/construct_1) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈstrʌkt/` · **US:** `/kənˈstrʌkt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconstruct__gb_3.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconstruct__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - construct something The building was constructed in 1993.
  - construct something out of something They constructed a shelter out of fallen branches.
  - construct something from something The frame is constructed from lightweight aluminium.
  - construct something of something On the smaller islands, houses are often constructed of local materials.

### [construction](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/construction) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈstrʌkʃn/` · **US:** `/kənˈstrʌkʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconstruction__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconstruction__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Construction began this year and will take approximately 18 months.
  - the costs of road construction and maintenance
  - Work has begun on the construction of the new airport.
  - the construction of a new database
  - under construction Our new offices are still under construction (= being built).
  - during construction Ethernet cabling was installed during construction.
  - the construction industry
  - construction work/workers
  - a construction company/firm
  - construction projects/costs/materials

### [consult](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/consult) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈsʌlt/` · **US:** `/kənˈsʌlt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsult__gb_3.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsult__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - consult somebody If the pain continues, consult your doctor.
  - consult somebody about something Have you consulted your lawyer about this?
  - a consulting engineer (= one who has expert knowledge and gives advice)
  - (North American English) consult with somebody (about/on something) Consult with your physician about possible treatments.

### [consultant](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/consultant) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈsʌltənt/` · **US:** `/kənˈsʌltənt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsultant__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsultant__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - a technology/design consultant
  - She is clearly being coached by image consultants.
  - consultant on something the president’s consultant on economic affairs
  - consultant to somebody/something He was happy to act as a consultant to the company.

### [consumption](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/consumption) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈsʌmpʃn/` · **US:** `/kənˈsʌmpʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsumption__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcons/xconsumption__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - the production of fuel for domestic consumption (= to be used in the country where it is produced)
  - Gas and oil consumption always increases in cold weather.
  - The meat was declared unfit for human consumption.
  - He was advised to reduce his alcohol consumption.
  - consumption of something Doctors say that children need to increase their consumption of fruit and vegetables.
  - (figurative) Her speech to party members was not intended for public consumption (= to be heard by the public).

### [contemporary](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/contemporary_1) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈtemprəri/` · **US:** `/kənˈtempəreri/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcont/xcontemporary__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcont/xcontemporary__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - We have no contemporary account of the battle (= written near the time that it happened).
  - contemporary with somebody/something He was contemporary with the dramatist Congreve.
  - The amphitheatre is roughly contemporary with the Colosseum in Rome.

### [contest](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/contest_1) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈkɒntest/` · **US:** `/ˈkɑːntest/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcont/xcontest__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcont/xcontest__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - to hold a singing/talent contest
  - to enter/win a contest
  - in a contest She was awarded the first prize in an essay contest .
  - contest between A and B It was a close contest between two evenly matched crews.
  - contest with somebody He said he had enjoyed the contest with his rival for the title .
  - contest to do something a contest to win a free tickets to the concert

### [contest](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/contest_2) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈtest/` · **US:** `/kənˈtest/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcont/xcontest__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcont/xcontest__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Three candidates contested the leadership.
  - The party has decided not to contest this election.
  - Conservatives met to decide who would contest the seat for them at the next election.
  - a hotly/fiercely/keenly contested game (= one in which the players try very hard to win and the scores are close)

### [contract](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/contract_1) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈkɒntrækt/` · **US:** `/ˈkɑːntrækt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcont/xcontract__gb_3.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcont/xcontract__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - All employees have a written contract of employment.
  - a research/modelling/recording contract
  - a lucrative government contract
  - contract with somebody to enter into/negotiate/sign a contract with the supplier
  - contract between A and B These clauses form part of the contract between buyer and seller.
  - contract for something a contract for the supply of vehicles
  - contract to do something to win/be awarded a contract to build a new school
  - to renew/extend/terminate/cancel a contract
  - on a contract I was on a three-year contract that expired last week.
  - under contract to/with somebody/something She is under contract to (= has a contract to work for) a major American computer firm.
  - out of contract The phone costs several hundred dollars more out of contract (= without a contract with a phone company).
  - The midfielder will be out of contract at the end of the season (= his contract with his club will have finished).
  - a contract worker (= one employed on a contract for a fixed period of time)
  - Under the terms of the contract the job should have been finished yesterday.
  - They were sued for breach of contract (= not doing what they agreed to do in a contract).
  - He had a release clause written into his contract.
  - subject to contract The offer has been accepted, subject to contract (= the agreement is not official until the contract is signed).

### [contract](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/contract_2) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/kənˈtrækt/` · **US:** `/kənˈtrækt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcont/xcontract__gb_4.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcont/xcontract__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Glass contracts as it cools.
  - The universe is expanding rather than contracting.
  - a contracting market
  - The economy will contract by 2 per cent this year.
  - The heart muscles contract to expel the blood.
  - contract something The exercise consists of stretching and contracting the leg muscles.
  - contract something to something ‘I will’ and ‘I shall’ are usually contracted to ‘I'll’ (= made shorter).

### [contribute](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/contribute) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/ˈkɒntrɪbjuːt/` · **US:** `/kənˈtrɪbjuːt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcont/xcontribute__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcont/xcontribute__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Do you wish to contribute?
  - contribute to/towards something Would you like to contribute to our collection?
  - to contribute to your pension
  - contribute something Check with your financial planner to make sure that you are contributing the correct amounts.
  - contribute something to/towards something We contributed £5 000 to the earthquake fund.

### [contribution](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/contribution) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˌkɒntrɪˈbjuːʃn/` · **US:** `/ˌkɑːntrɪˈbjuːʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcont/xcontribution__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcont/xcontribution__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - All contributions will be gratefully received.
  - We rely entirely on voluntary contributions.
  - campaign contributions
  - contribution to something to make a substantial contribution to charity
  - contribution towards something valuable contributions towards the upkeep of the cathedral
  - contribution towards doing something She argued that a greater contribution towards reducing Britain's record debts should be asked of the better off.
  - contribution from/by somebody/something Financial contributions from individuals paid for office and printing expenses.

### [controversial](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/controversial) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/ˌkɒntrəˈvɜːʃl/` · **US:** `/ˌkɑːntrəˈvɜːrʃl/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/x/xco/xcont/xcontroversial__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/x/xco/xcont/xcontroversial__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**

### [criticism](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/criticism) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈkrɪtɪsɪzəm/` · **US:** `/ˈkrɪtɪsɪzəm/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/c/cri/criti/criticism__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/c/cri/criti/criticism__us_3.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - to draw/face/receive criticism
  - The plan has attracted criticism from consumer groups.
  - She sought to deflect criticism by blaming her family.
  - People in public life must always be open to criticism (= willing to accept being criticized).
  - Ben is very sensitive—he just can't take criticism.
  - to offer somebody constructive criticism (= that is meant to be helpful)
  - I didn't mean it as a criticism.
  - criticisms levelled at (= aimed at) journalists
  - criticism of somebody/something There was widespread criticism of the government's handling of the disaster.
  - My only criticism of the house is that it is on a main road.
  - He was clearly stung by media criticism of his previous statement.
  - criticism over something The former minister is facing growing criticism over his remark.
  - The government came under heavy criticism over its policies.
  - We came in for some sharp criticism over this decision.
  - criticism for something The actress has come under criticism for her comments about her co-stars.
  - The film star faced a barrage of criticism for his behaviour.
  - criticism about something The actor has recently faced harsh criticism about his weight.
  - criticism against somebody/something The past five years has seen growing criticism against the regime.

### [criticize](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/criticize) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/ˈkrɪtɪsaɪz/` · **US:** `/ˈkrɪtɪsaɪz/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/c/cri/criti/criticize__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/c/cri/criti/criticize__us_3.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - All you ever do is criticize!
  - criticize somebody/something The decision was harshly criticized by environmental groups.
  - a heavily criticized plan
  - Journalists who strongly criticize the government can be heavily fined or imprisoned.
  - criticize somebody/something for something She has been sharply criticized for her comments.
  - The government has been criticized for not taking the problem seriously.
  - criticize somebody/something over something The company has been criticized over its handling of the contract.
  - criticize somebody/something as + adj. The law was widely criticized as racist.
  - criticize somebody/something as something The project has been criticized as a waste of money.

### [decline](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/decline_1) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈklaɪn/` · **US:** `/dɪˈklaɪn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dec/decli/decline__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dec/decli/decline__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Support for the party continues to decline.
  - decline by something Sales of whole milk declined by 4 per cent.
  - decline in something The city declined in importance in the nineteenth century.
  - to decline in popularity/value/number
  - Jobs in manufacturing have steadily declined.
  - to decline sharply/significantly/dramatically
  - to decline rapidly/markedly/substantially
  - Her health began to decline.

### [decoration](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/decoration) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˌdekəˈreɪʃn/` · **US:** `/ˌdekəˈreɪʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dec/decor/decoration__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dec/decor/decoration__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Christmas/festive decorations
  - Halloween decorations hung from every corner.
  - cake/table decorations
  - We made our own decorations.
  - Floral decorations adorned the church.
  - The decorations were taken down and put away for another year.

### [decrease](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/decrease_2) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈdiːkriːs/` · **US:** `/ˈdiːkriːs/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dec/decre/decrease__gb_3.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dec/decre/decrease__us_3_rr.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Sales for May show a decrease compared with the same month last year.
  - decrease in something There has been some decrease in military spending this year.
  - a decrease in the number/level/rate of something
  - There has been a dramatic decrease in activity among our kids.
  - decrease of something (in something) There has been a decrease of nearly 6 per cent in the number of visitors to the museum.
  - decrease (from something) (to something) a decrease from 62% to just under half
  - on the decrease Marriage is still on the decrease (= decreasing).

### [decrease](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/decrease_1) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈkriːs/` · **US:** `/dɪˈkriːs/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dec/decre/decrease__gb_4.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dec/decre/decrease__us_4_rr.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Donations have decreased significantly over the past few years.
  - a decreasing population
  - decrease (from something) (to something) The number of new students decreased from 210 to 160 this year.
  - decrease by something The price of wheat has decreased by 5 per cent.
  - decrease in something This species of bird is decreasing in numbers every year.
  - to decrease in size/value
  - decrease with something Fertility decreases with age.
  - decrease something The drug did not significantly decrease the risk of heart attack.
  - People should decrease the amount of fat they eat.
  - to decrease the incidence/likelihood/rate of something

### [deeply](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/deeply) *(adverb)*
- **UK:** `/ˈdiːpli/` · **US:** `/ˈdiːpli/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dee/deepl/deeply__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dee/deepl/deeply__us_3.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - She is deeply religious.
  - His art was deeply personal.
  - This is a deeply disturbing film.
  - a deeply unpopular decision
  - I deeply regret my error.
  - Farmers care deeply for their land.
  - We are deeply grateful for your support.
  - Memories of the war are deeply rooted in people's minds.
  - deeply held beliefs/convictions/views

### [defeat](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/defeat_2) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈfiːt/` · **US:** `/dɪˈfiːt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/def/defea/defeat__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/def/defea/defeat__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The party faces defeat in the election.
  - They suffered a narrow defeat in the final.
  - a heavy/humiliating/crushing defeat
  - The world champion has only had two defeats in 20 fights.
  - They finally had to admit defeat (= stop trying to be successful).
  - to concede/accept defeat
  - defeat by somebody their defeat by the Brazilians
  - defeat against somebody last week's defeat against Manchester United
  - a punishing defeat at the hands of Iceland in the World Cup
  - in defeat He was gracious in defeat, acknowledging his opponent's greater skill.
  - a series of small victories and defeats

### [defeat](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/defeat_1) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈfiːt/` · **US:** `/dɪˈfiːt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/def/defea/defeat__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/def/defea/defeat__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - defeat somebody/something He defeated the champion in three sets.
  - to defeat a rival/an opponent
  - The goal is to defeat the enemy by whatever means possible.
  - a defeated army
  - Garibaldi defeated the Neapolitan army.
  - defeat somebody by something The government was defeated by 200 votes to 83.
  - Davis defeated Morris by eight points in the semi-final.
  - defeat somebody in something Our team was narrowly defeated in the final.
  - It was said that he could not be defeated in battle.

### [defence](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/defence) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈfens/` · **US:** `/dɪˈfens/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/def/defen/defence__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/def/defen/defence__us_12.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - in defence of somebody/something soldiers who died in defence of their country
  - What points can be raised in defence of this argument?
  - in somebody's defence I have to say in her defence that she knew nothing about it beforehand.
  - When her brother was criticized she leapt to his defence.
  - to spring/jump/rush to the defence of somebody/something

### [defend](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/defend) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈfend/` · **US:** `/dɪˈfend/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/def/defen/defend__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/def/defen/defend__us_4.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - defend somebody/something The role of the military is to defend the country.
  - Troops have been sent to defend the borders.
  - defend somebody/something against somebody/something The male birds defend their territory against other males.
  - defend somebody/something from somebody/something The cannons once defended the city from attack by sea.
  - defend yourself (from/against somebody/something) All our officers are trained to defend themselves against knife attacks.
  - defend against somebody/something It is impossible to defend against an all-out attack.

### [defender](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/defender) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈfendə(r)/` · **US:** `/dɪˈfendər/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/def/defen/defender__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/def/defen/defender__us_1.mp3)

### [delay](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/delay_1) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈleɪ/` · **US:** `/dɪˈleɪ/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/del/delay/delay__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/del/delay/delay__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Commuters will face long delays on the roads today.
  - to experience/suffer delays
  - to avoid/minimize further delays
  - Increased congestion and traffic delays are expected.
  - a delay of two hours/a two-hour delay
  - delay in something The strike has led to some delays in train services.
  - delay in doing something We apologize for the delay in answering your letter.
  - delay to something These issues have caused serious delays to the project.
  - Flights to New York may be subject to delay.

### [delay](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/delay_2) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈleɪ/` · **US:** `/dɪˈleɪ/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/del/delay/delay__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/del/delay/delay__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - My flight was delayed.
  - Thousands of commuters were delayed for over an hour.
  - The government is accused of using delaying tactics (= deliberately doing something to delay a process, decision, etc.).
  - What could have delayed him?

### [delete](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/delete_1) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈliːt/` · **US:** `/dɪˈliːt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/del/delet/delete__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/del/delet/delete__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Your name has been deleted from the list.
  - This command deletes files from the directory.
  - (British English) Mr/Mrs/Ms (delete as appropriate)
  - Delete the word ‘it’ and insert ‘them’.

### [deliberate](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/deliberate_1) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈlɪbərət/` · **US:** `/dɪˈlɪbərət/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/del/delib/deliberate__gb_4.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/del/delib/deliberate__us_2_rr.mp3)
- **Examples:**

  - The speech was a deliberate attempt to embarrass the government.
  - a deliberate lie/deception

### [deliberately](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/deliberately) *(adverb)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈlɪbərətli/` · **US:** `/dɪˈlɪbərətli/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/del/delib/deliberately__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/del/delib/deliberately__us_2_rr.mp3)
- **Examples:**

  - an ad campaign that deliberately targets children
  - She was accused of deliberately misleading Parliament.
  - to deliberately withhold/conceal information
  - The fire had been started deliberately.
  - Her tone was deliberately insulting.

### [delight](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/delight_1) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈlaɪt/` · **US:** `/dɪˈlaɪt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/del/delig/delight__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/del/delig/delight__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - a feeling of sheer/pure delight
  - with delight The children squealed with delight when they saw the puppy.
  - to the delight of somebody | to somebody's delight She won the game easily, to the delight of all her fans.
  - delight in doing something He takes (great) delight in (= enjoys) proving others wrong.
  - delight in something She took a simple delight in joys that we could all share.
  - delight at something She couldn't hide her delight at the news.
  - delight at doing something He expressed his delight at seeing us all again.

### [delight](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/delight_2) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈlaɪt/` · **US:** `/dɪˈlaɪt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/del/delig/delight__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/del/delig/delight__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - This news will delight his fans all over the world.
  - a movie that will thrill and delight most audiences
  - Her lack of reserve delighted him.
  - She had a limitless capacity to astonish and delight.

### [delighted](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/delighted) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈlaɪtɪd/` · **US:** `/dɪˈlaɪtɪd/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/del/delig/delighted__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/del/delig/delighted__us_3.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - a delighted smile
  - delighted to do something I'd be absolutely delighted to come.
  - ‘Can you stay for dinner?’ ‘I’d be delighted (to)!’
  - delighted that… I was delighted that you could stay.
  - delighted by something She was delighted by the news of the wedding.
  - delighted at something They were highly delighted at the court's decision.
  - delighted with something I was delighted with my presents.
  - delighted about something We are delighted about the decision.
  - delighted for somebody I was so pleased and delighted for him when he started losing weight.

### [delivery](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/delivery) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈlɪvəri/` · **US:** `/dɪˈlɪvəri/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/del/deliv/delivery__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/del/deliv/delivery__us_1_rr.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - Allow 28 days for delivery.
  - We offer free delivery on orders over $200.
  - The service guarantees next day delivery.
  - on delivery Please pay for goods on delivery (= when you receive them).
  - (formal) When can you take delivery of (= be available to receive) the car?
  - A delivery van was waiting in the street outside.

### [demand](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/demand_1) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈmɑːnd/` · **US:** `/dɪˈmænd/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dem/deman/demand__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dem/deman/demand__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - demand for something a demand for higher pay
  - demand that… demands that the law on gun ownership should be changed
  - A federal judge rejected their demands.
  - The management had no intention of meeting union demands.

### [demand](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/demand_2) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈmɑːnd/` · **US:** `/dɪˈmænd/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dem/deman/demand__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dem/deman/demand__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - demand something They are demanding the release of all political prisoners.
  - You should demand an apology in writing.
  - Protesters demanded the resignation of the prime minister.
  - demand that… The UN has demanded that all troops be withdrawn.
  - (British English also) They are demanding that all troops should be withdrawn.
  - The judge demanded that we turn off our phones.
  - demand to do something I demand to see the manager.
  - demand something of somebody We demand a lot of our teachers.
  - demand something from somebody He had demanded money from her.

### [democracy](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/democracy) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈmɒkrəsi/` · **US:** `/dɪˈmɑːkrəsi/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dem/democ/democracy__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dem/democ/democracy__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - parliamentary democracy
  - the principles of democracy

### [democratic](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/democratic) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/ˌdeməˈkrætɪk/` · **US:** `/ˌdeməˈkrætɪk/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dem/democ/democratic__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dem/democ/democratic__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - a democratic country
  - a democratic system
  - democratic government
  - They are aiming to make the institutions of the EU truly democratic.
  - Exercise your democratic right to vote.

### [demonstrate](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/demonstrate) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/ˈdemənstreɪt/` · **US:** `/ˈdemənstreɪt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dem/demon/demonstrate__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dem/demon/demonstrate__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - demonstrate that… New research convincingly demonstrates that age-related memory loss is not inevitable.
  - demonstrate something These paintings demonstrate his extraordinary ability as a portrait painter.
  - The award demonstrated the importance that local people place on road safety.
  - This new anthology amply demonstrates the range and vitality of modern Scottish poetry.
  - demonstrate how, what, etc… This study clearly demonstrates how fishing can affect an ecosystem.
  - demonstrate something to somebody Let me demonstrate to you some of the difficulties we are facing.
  - demonstrate somebody/something to be something The theories were demonstrated to be false.
  - it is demonstrated that… It has been demonstrated that this drug is effective.

### [demonstration](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/demonstration) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˌdemənˈstreɪʃn/` · **US:** `/ˌdemənˈstreɪʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dem/demon/demonstration__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dem/demon/demonstration__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - to take part in/go on a demonstration
  - to hold/stage a demonstration
  - mass demonstrations in support of the exiled leader
  - anti-government demonstrations
  - a peaceful/violent demonstration

### [deny](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/deny) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈnaɪ/` · **US:** `/dɪˈnaɪ/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/den/deny_/deny__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/den/deny_/deny__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - deny something to deny an allegation/a charge/an accusation
  - He has denied any involvement in the incident.
  - The company strongly denies wrongdoing.
  - to vehemently/strenuously/categorically deny something
  - A spokesperson refused to either confirm or deny the reports.
  - deny (that)… She denied that there had been a cover-up.
  - It can't be denied that we need to devote more resources to this problem.
  - There's no denying the fact that quicker action could have saved them.
  - deny doing something He denies knowing anything about the plot.

### [depart](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/depart) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈpɑːt/` · **US:** `/dɪˈpɑːrt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dep/depar/depart__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dep/depar/depart__us_1.mp3)

### [dependent](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/dependent_1) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈpendənt/` · **US:** `/dɪˈpendənt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dep/depen/dependent__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dep/depen/dependent__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**

### [deposit](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/deposit_1) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈpɒzɪt/` · **US:** `/dɪˈpɑːzɪt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dep/depos/deposit__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dep/depos/deposit__us_1.mp3)

### [depressed](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/depressed) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈprest/` · **US:** `/dɪˈprest/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dep/depre/depressed__gb_4.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dep/depre/depressed__us_1.mp3)

  - depressed at something He was really depressed at the thought of going into the office.
  - depressed over something She was depressed over the recent death of her mother.
  - depressed by something I was depressed by our lack of progress.

### [depressing](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/depressing) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈpresɪŋ/` · **US:** `/dɪˈpresɪŋ/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dep/depre/depressing__gb_3.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dep/depre/depressing__us_1.mp3)

### [depression](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/depression) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈpreʃn/` · **US:** `/dɪˈpreʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dep/depre/depression__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dep/depre/depression__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - She was diagnosed as having clinical depression.
  - She suffered from severe depression after losing her job.

### [depth](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/depth) *(noun)*

  - in depth The oil well extended several hundreds of feet in depth.

### [deserve](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/deserve) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈzɜːv/` · **US:** `/dɪˈzɜːrv/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/des/deser/deserve__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/des/deser/deserve__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**

  - to deserve praise/respect

### [desire](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/desire_1) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈzaɪə(r)/` · **US:** `/dɪˈzaɪər/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/des/desir/desire__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/des/desir/desire__us_1.mp3)

  - (formal) I have no desire (= I do not want) to discuss the matter further.
  - He has expressed a desire to see you.
  - (formal) desire that… his father's desire that he become a lawyer

### [desire](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/desire_2) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/dɪˈzaɪə(r)/` · **US:** `/dɪˈzaɪər/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/des/desir/desire__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/des/desir/desire__us_1.mp3)

  - The dessert can be topped with cream, if desired (= if you like).
  - The medicine did not achieve the desired effect.
  - desire to do something Fewer people desire to live in the north of the country.
  - desire somebody to do something She desired him to leave her alone.

### [disagreement](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/disagreement) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˌdɪsəˈɡriːmənt/` · **US:** `/ˌdɪsəˈɡriːmənt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/d/dis/disag/disagreement__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/d/dis/disag/disagreement__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**

### [disappoint](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/disappoint) *(verb)*

  - emphasis on/upon doing something The emphasis is very much on learning the spoken language.
  - There is too much emphasis on reducing costs.

  - There has been a shift of emphasis from manufacturing to service industries.
  - The course has a vocational emphasis.

  - emphasize how, what, etc… He emphasized how little was known about the disease.
  - it must/should be emphasized that… It should be emphasized that this is only one possible explanation.
  - + speech ‘This must be our top priority,’ he emphasized.

  - She never lost her enthusiasm for teaching.
  - enthusiasm for doing something He has shown little or no enthusiasm for regulating financial markets before now.

### [enthusiastic](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/enthusiastic) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/ɪnˌθjuːziˈæstɪk/` · **US:** `/ɪnˌθuːziˈæstɪk/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/e/ent/enthu/enthusiastic__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/e/ent/enthu/enthusiastic__us_4.mp3)

### [entirely](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/entirely) *(adverb)*

### [equip](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/equip) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/ɪˈkwɪp/` · **US:** `/ɪˈkwɪp/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/e/equ/equip/equip__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/e/equ/equip/equip__us_1.mp3)

### [equivalent](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/equivalent_2) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/ɪˈkwɪvələnt/` · **US:** `/ɪˈkwɪvələnt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/e/equ/equiv/equivalent__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/e/equ/equiv/equivalent__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - 250 grams or an equivalent amount in ounces
  - the price we would pay elsewhere for a broadly equivalent house
  - equivalent to something Eight kilometres is roughly equivalent to five miles.
  - The new regulation was seen as equivalent to censorship.

### [equivalent](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/equivalent_1) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ɪˈkwɪvələnt/` · **US:** `/ɪˈkwɪvələnt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/e/equ/equiv/equivalent__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/e/equ/equiv/equivalent__us_1.mp3)

  - equivalent of doing something Breathing such polluted air is the equivalent of (= has the same effect as) smoking ten cigarettes a day.
  - equivalent to something The German ‘Gymnasium’ is the closest equivalent to the grammar school in England.

### [era](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/era) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈɪərə/` · **US:** `/ˈerə/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/e/era/era__/era__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/e/era/era__/era__us_1_rr.mp3)

### [erupt](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/erupt) *(verb)*

- **Examples:**

### [essentially](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/essentially) *(adverb)*
- **UK:** `/ɪˈsenʃəli/` · **US:** `/ɪˈsenʃəli/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/e/ess/essen/essentially__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/e/ess/essen/essentially__us_1.mp3)

### [establish](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/establish) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/ɪˈstæblɪʃ/` · **US:** `/ɪˈstæblɪʃ/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/e/est/estab/establish__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/e/est/estab/establish__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**

  - The company established a base in Florida last year.
  - to establish a state/government/group/school
  - to establish standards/principles
  - Let’s establish some ground rules.
  - The proposal would establish a system of inspections of prisons worldwide.
  - They are establishing a network of pumps and pipelines to move the oil.
  - The new treaty establishes a free trade zone.

### [estate](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/estate) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ɪˈsteɪt/` · **US:** `/ɪˈsteɪt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/e/est/estat/estate__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/e/est/estat/estate__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**

### [estimate](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/estimate_2) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈestɪmət/` · **US:** `/ˈestɪmət/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/e/est/estim/estimate__gb_4.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/e/est/estim/estimate__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - to provide/obtain an estimate
  - estimate of something I can give you a rough estimate of the amount of wood you will need.
  - What is the latest estimate of the number of chimpanzees in the wild?
  - official government estimates of traffic growth over the next decade
  - a ballpark estimate (= an approximate estimate)
  - At least 5 000 people were killed, and that's a conservative estimate (= the real figure will be higher).
  - estimate for something Using this index would produce a lower estimate for the rate of inflation.
  - estimate from something The map is the best estimate from the data available.
  - according to an estimate Losses totalled $1.87 billion last year, according to estimates.

### [estimate](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/estimate_1) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/ˈestɪmeɪt/` · **US:** `/ˈestɪmeɪt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/e/est/estim/estimate__gb_3.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/e/est/estim/estimate__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - estimate something to estimate the cost/value/number of something
  - The satellite will cost an estimated £400 million.
  - estimate something at something Police estimate the crowd at 30 000.
  - estimate something from something All variables can be estimated from the data.
  - estimate something as something The number of breeding pairs was estimated as the number of pairs building nests.
  - estimate something to do something The deal is estimated to be worth around $1.5 million.
  - estimate (that)… We estimated (that) it would cost about €5 000.
  - it is estimated (that)… It is estimated (that) the project will last four years.
  - estimate how many, large, etc… It is hard to estimate how many children have dyslexia.

- **UK:** `/ɪˌvæljuˈeɪʃn/` · **US:** `/ɪˌvæljuˈeɪʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/e/eva/evalu/evaluation__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/e/eva/evalu/evaluation__us_1.mp3)

- **Examples:**

  - I tried desperately to think of a good excuse.
  - a lame/feeble/poor/flimsy excuse
  - a reasonable/valid excuse

  - excuse for something There's no excuse for such behaviour.
  - excuse for doing something His excuse for forgetting her birthday was that he had lost his diary.
  - You don't have to make excuses for her (= try to think of reasons for her behaviour).
  - It's late. I'm afraid I'll have to make my excuses (= say I'm sorry, give my reasons and leave).

### [excuse](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/excuse_2) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/ɪkˈskjuːz/` · **US:** `/ɪkˈskjuːz/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/e/exc/excus/excuse__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/e/exc/excus/excuse__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - excuse something Please excuse the mess.
  - excuse somebody You must excuse my father—he's not always that rude.
  - excuse somebody for something She had been excused for her actions.
  - excuse somebody for doing something I hope you'll excuse me for being so late.
  - (British English) You might be excused for thinking that Ben is in charge (= he is not, but it is an easy mistake to make).
  - excuse somebody doing something Excuse me interrupting you.
  - (formal) Excuse my interrupting you.
  - If you'll excuse me pointing this out, I think you've made a mistake here.

### [executive](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/executive_1) *(noun)*

### [exhibit](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/exhibit_1) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/ɪɡˈzɪbɪt/` · **US:** `/ɪɡˈzɪbɪt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/e/exh/exhib/exhibit__gb_3.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/e/exh/exhib/exhibit__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - exhibit something (at/in…) They will be exhibiting their new designs at the trade fairs.

### [existence](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/existence) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ɪɡˈzɪstəns/` · **US:** `/ɪɡˈzɪstəns/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/e/exi/exist/existence__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/e/exi/exist/existence__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - I was unaware of his existence until today.
  - to believe in the existence of God
  - the mystery of human existence
  - The continued existence of the industry depends on the investment of public money.
  - The peasants depend on a good harvest for their very existence (= in order to continue to live).
  - The mere existence of these strange creatures fascinated him.
  - Some groups in the industry seek to deny the existence of a global warming problem.
  - The school owed its existence to the generosity of one man.
  - Internet shopping constitutes a threat to the existence of high-street shops.
  - in existence The company has been in existence since 1924.
  - This is the oldest Hebrew manuscript in existence.
  - existence as something Pakistan came into existence as an independent country in 1947.
  - The book acknowledges the existence of graffiti as an art form.
  - Several species are in danger of being hunted out of existence.
  - There was a fear that the club might go out of existence for lack of support.

- **UK:** `/ˌekspekˈteɪʃn/` · **US:** `/ˌekspekˈteɪʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/e/exp/expec/expectation__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/e/exp/expec/expectation__us_1.mp3)

  - in expectation of something Buyers are holding back in expectation of further price cuts.
  - in expectation I applied for the post more in hope than expectation.
  - Contrary to expectations, interest rates did not rise.
  - Against all expectations, she was enjoying herself.

### [expense](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/expense) *(noun)*

### [illustration](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/illustration) *(noun)*

  - illustration for something He produced illustrations for children's books.

### [imagination](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/imagination) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ɪˌmædʒɪˈneɪʃn/` · **US:** `/ɪˌmædʒɪˈneɪʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/i/ima/imagi/imagination__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/i/ima/imagi/imagination__us_1.mp3)

  - in your imagination Nobody hates you—it's all in your imagination.
  - This is an image which persists in the popular imagination.
  - (informal) Use your imagination! (= used to tell somebody that they will have to guess the answer to the question they have asked you, usually because it is obvious or embarrassing)

- **UK:** `/ɪmˈprest/` · **US:** `/ɪmˈprest/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/i/imp/impre/impressed__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/i/imp/impre/impressed__us_1.mp3)

### [incident](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/incident_1) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈɪnsɪdənt/` · **US:** `/ˈɪnsɪdənt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/i/inc/incid/incident__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/i/inc/incid/incident__us_1.mp3)

### [income](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/income) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈɪnkəm/` · **US:** `/ˈɪnkəm/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/i/inc/incom/income__gb_3.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/i/inc/incom/income__us_1_rr.mp3)

### [infection](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/infection) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ɪnˈfekʃn/` · **US:** `/ɪnˈfekʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/i/inf/infec/infection__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/i/inf/infec/infection__us_3.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - to cause/prevent infection
  - Vaccination is essential to protect people exposed to hepatitis B infection.
  - The drugs slow down the progression of HIV infection.
  - Bacterial infection of the wound may occur.
  - to increase the risk of infection
  - The rate of infection is highest in the north-west of the country.

### [maintain](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/maintain) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/meɪnˈteɪn/` · **US:** `/meɪnˈteɪn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/m/mai/maint/maintain__gb_3.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/m/mai/maint/maintain__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - to maintain law and order/standards/a balance/control
  - ANU has maintained its position as Australia's top university.
  - The two countries have always maintained close relations.
  - (formal) She maintained a dignified silence.
  - to maintain prices (= prevent them from falling or rising)

### [majority](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/majority) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/məˈdʒɒrəti/` · **US:** `/məˈdʒɔːrəti/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/m/maj/major/majority__gb_3.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/m/maj/major/majority__us_3_rr.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - majority (of somebody/something) The majority of people interviewed prefer TV to radio.
  - The majority was/were in favour of banning smoking.
  - This treatment is not available in the vast majority of hospitals.
  - The overwhelming majority of participants were men.
  - to represent/form/constitute/comprise the majority of somebody/something
  - in a/the majority (of something) In the nursing profession, women are in the majority.
  - The drug provided significant pain relief in a majority of cases.
  - a majority decision (= one that is decided by what most people want)
  - We make decisions by majority vote.
  - the majority opinion/view

### [observation](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/observation) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˌɒbzəˈveɪʃn/` · **US:** `/ˌɑːbzərˈveɪʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/o/obs/obser/observation__gb_3.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/o/obs/obser/observation__us_1_rr.mp3)
- **Examples:**

  - under observation The suspect is being kept under observation (= watched closely by the police).
  - She has outstanding powers of observation (= the ability to notice things around her).
  - an observation post/tower (= a place from where somebody, especially an enemy, can be watched)
  - an observation deck (= a room or platform at the top of a tall building which provides views of the surrounding area)

### [observe](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/observe) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əbˈzɜːv/` · **US:** `/əbˈzɜːrv/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/o/obs/obser/observe__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/o/obs/obser/observe__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - observe somebody/something Have you observed any changes lately?
  - All the characters in the novel are closely observed (= seem like people in real life).
  - I want you to observe all the details.
  - The patterns observed in our study may represent a general rule.
  - observe somebody/something do something The police observed a man enter the bank.
  - observe somebody/something doing something They observed him entering the bank.
  - observe that… She observed that all the chairs were already occupied.
  - be observed to do something He was observed to follow her closely.

### [observer](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/observer) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/əbˈzɜːvə(r)/` · **US:** `/əbˈzɜːrvər/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/o/obs/obser/observer__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/o/obs/obser/observer__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - According to observers, the plane exploded shortly after take-off.
  - To the casual observer (= somebody who does not pay much attention), the system appears confusing.
  - Most art forms require a contribution from the observer.

### [obstacle](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/obstacle) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈɒbstəkl/` · **US:** `/ˈɑːbstəkl/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/o/obs/obsta/obstacle__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/o/obs/obsta/obstacle__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - So far, we have managed to overcome all the obstacles that have been placed in our path.
  - obstacle to doing something A lack of qualifications can be a major obstacle to finding a job.
  - obstacle to somebody doing something The MP claims that there is now no obstacle to him standing at the next general election.
  - obstacle to something The huge distances involved have proved an obstacle to communication between villages.

### [obtain](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/obtain) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əbˈteɪn/` · **US:** `/əbˈteɪn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/o/obt/obtai/obtain__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/o/obt/obtai/obtain__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - to obtain information/data/results
  - I've been trying to obtain permission to publish this material.
  - I finally managed to obtain a copy of the report.
  - Further details can be obtained by writing to the above address.
  - To obtain the overall score, add up the totals in each column.

### [occasionally](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/occasionally) *(adverb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈkeɪʒnəli/` · **US:** `/əˈkeɪʒnəli/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/o/occ/occas/occasionally__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/o/occ/occas/occasionally__us_3.mp3)
- **Examples:**

  - This type of allergy can very occasionally be fatal.
  - Only occasionally was there any doubt that they would succeed.
  - Johnston is an intelligent, occasionally brilliant writer.
  - Cook on a medium heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.

### [occupation](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/occupation) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˌɒkjuˈpeɪʃn/` · **US:** `/ˌɑːkjuˈpeɪʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/o/occ/occup/occupation__gb_3.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/o/occ/occup/occupation__us_1.mp3)

### [occupy](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/occupy) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/ˈɒkjupaɪ/` · **US:** `/ˈɑːkjupaɪ/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/o/occ/occup/occupy__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/o/occ/occup/occupy__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - The bed seemed to occupy most of the room.
  - As the company grew, it continued to occupy more space.
  - Administrative work occupies half of my time.
  - How do you occupy your time?
  - Their time is fully occupied with their rigorous training regime.

### [offence](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/offence) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/əˈfens/` · **US:** `/əˈfens/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/o/off/offen/offence__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/o/off/offen/offence__us_5.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - a criminal/serious/minor/sexual offence
  - a drug/firearms/traffic offence

  - a capital offence (= one for which somebody may be punished by death)
  - What are the alleged offences (= that have been stated but not yet proved)?
  - He was not aware that he had committed an offence.
  - New legislation makes it an offence to carry guns.
  - He was found guilty of offences under the Official Secrets Act.
  - These people have been charged with public order offences.
  - He has been arrested for a serious offence.
  - offence against somebody/something an offence against society/humanity/the state
  - prisoners convicted of offences against children

### [offend](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/offend) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/əˈfend/` · **US:** `/əˈfend/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/o/off/offen/offend__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/o/off/offen/offend__us_2.mp3)

- **UK:** `/əˈpəʊz/` · **US:** `/əˈpəʊz/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/o/opp/oppos/oppose__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/o/opp/oppos/oppose__us_2.mp3)

### [opposition](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/opposition) *(noun)*

  - The army met with fierce opposition in every town.
  - The proposal faced stiff opposition.
  - We cannot back down at the first sign of opposition.
  - opposition forces (= people who are arguing, fighting, etc. with another group)

  - a pension scheme/plan

### [perceive](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/perceive) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/pəˈsiːv/` · **US:** `/pərˈsiːv/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/p/per/perce/perceive__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/p/per/perce/perceive__us_1.mp3)

  - I do not perceive myself as an expert.
  - A science degree and artistic interests are often perceived as incompatible.
  - perceive somebody/something to be/have something They were widely perceived to have been unlucky.

### [perception](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/perception) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/pəˈsepʃn/` · **US:** `/pərˈsepʃn/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/p/per/perce/perception__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/p/per/perce/perception__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**

### [permanent](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/permanent_1) *(adjective)*
- **UK:** `/ˈpɜːmənənt/` · **US:** `/ˈpɜːrmənənt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/p/per/perma/permanent__gb_4.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/p/per/perma/permanent__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**

  - The gallery hosts various exhibitions and a permanent collection.
  - We decided to make the arrangement permanent.

### [permanently](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/permanently) *(adverb)*
- **UK:** `/ˈpɜːmənəntli/` · **US:** `/ˈpɜːrmənəntli/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/p/per/perma/permanently__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/p/per/perma/permanently__us_1.mp3)

### [permit](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/permit_2) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/ˈpɜːmɪt/` · **US:** `/ˈpɜːrmɪt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/p/per/permi/permit__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/p/per/permi/permit__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - a parking/building permit
  - to apply for a permit
  - permit for something The agency issued permits for exploratory drilling.
  - The company failed to obtain the necessary permits for the landfill project.
  - You cannot enter the military base without a permit.

### [permit](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/permit_1) *(verb)*
- **UK:** `/pəˈmɪt/` · **US:** `/pərˈmɪt/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/p/per/permi/permit__gb_1.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/p/per/permi/permit__us_1.mp3)
- **Examples:**
  - be permitted Mobile phones are not permitted in the examination room.
  - be permitted something We were not permitted any contact with each other.
  - be permitted to do something Visitors are not permitted to take photographs.
  - permit something The owners have been unwilling to permit the use of their land.
  - There are fines for exceeding permitted levels of noise pollution.
  - permit somebody/yourself something Jim permitted himself a wry smile.
  - permit somebody/yourself to do something The bill was designed to permit new fathers to take time off work.
  - She would not permit herself to look at them.
  - (formal) Permit me to offer you some advice.

### [perspective](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/perspective) *(noun)*
- **UK:** `/pəˈspektɪv/` · **US:** `/pərˈspektɪv/` · [🔊 UK Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/uk_pron/p/per/persp/perspective__gb_2.mp3) | [🔊 US Audio](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/media/english/us_pron/p/per/persp/perspective__us_2.mp3)
- **Examples:**

  - from a… perspective Try to see the issue from a different perspective.
  - from the perspective of somebody/something a report that looks at the education system from the perspective of deaf people
  - perspective on something The exhibition provides us with a unique perspective on her work.

  - His anxiety about the work was just a passing phase.

### [phenomenon](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/phenomenon) *(noun)*
